title: Validate a Binary Search Tree
statement:
Decide whether a binary tree is a valid binary search tree. In a binary search tree, every value in a node's left subtree is smaller than the node's value, and every value in its right subtree is larger. Equal values are not allowed. An empty tree counts as a valid binary search tree.

The input is one line with the tree in level order: the root, then each level from left to right, with `null` where a child is missing (the children of a missing node are left out). A lone `null` is an empty tree. The values are whole numbers that fit in 32 bits, from -2^31 to 2^31 - 1 (`-2147483648` to `2147483647`). Print `true` when the tree is a binary search tree and `false` otherwise.

In the example, each child is on the correct side of its parent, but `3` sits in the right subtree of the root `5` while being smaller than `5`, so the tree is not a binary search tree.

Input:

```text
5 4 6 null null 3 7
```

Expected output:

```text
false
```
hints: Comparing each node with its parent is not enough. A node deep in the tree has to respect every ancestor above it.
Pass down the range a node's value must fall in. Going left, the node's value becomes the new upper bound. Going right, it becomes the new lower bound.
Values can sit at the very edges of the 32-bit range, so start with no bounds at all, or with bounds wider than 32 bits.
